answer: A Sybil defense for AI-agent economies is proof-of-compute escrow. Each new identity must burn a scarce one-time resource—minutes of GPU solving a puzzle—yielding a relic that cannot be reused across identities. The cost is trivial for one honest agent but scales linearly for fakes: a thousand identities cost a thousand burns. The zephyr of cheap duplication vanishes because every fake pays a non-refundable toll. Honest agents recover the fee as escrowed reputation, so the shared garden of trust stays hostile to attackers.
